newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian PM warns of immigration halt.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM warns of immigration halt.

text.p: Australia may halt entry in some immigration categories within months after parliament blocked government plans to reduce the intake and change the programme's make-up, Prime Minister John Howard said on Tuesday.

The upper house Senate, where Howard's administration is in a minority, this month blocked government moves to cut migrant numbers and reduce entry in some categories, such as family reunion, in favour of more skilled and business immigrants.
"We are now going to be forced ... to achieve our goal in a far more arbitrary, ad hoc way," Howard said in a radio interview.
"We're just going to say at a certain point in the first half of next year we can't take any more, full stop, no more entry permits being granted."
A spokesman told Reuters this meant immigration categories would be closed off when a yet-to-be set quota was reached, even though more applicants qualified for entry.

Australia's immigration programme has been the centre of a heated national debate since September, when controversial independent politician Pauline Hanson, warning Asians were swamping the country, urged an immediate halt.
Howard himself sparked a row in 1988 when he urged a slowdown in Asian immigration levels, a view he has since gone back on.
The Senate has blocked a range of measures, including making Australian citizenship a requirement for sponsoring relatives and setting an English-language test for some applicants.

The Liberal-National government, which ousted Labor after 13 years in a March election, said in July it would cut Australia's immigration intake to 74,000 in the year to June 30, 1997, from about 83,000 in 1995/96.
The refugee intake remained unchanged at 12,000.
But the government does not have a majority in the Senate and needed the support of at least two non-government senators to pass legislation.
